text:
anna_support: FYI customer MapleHealth just opened a support ticket — p95 for realtime API jumped from ~420ms to ~1.8s after the byte-encoder cutover. They see it on long inputs > 6k chars.

anna_support: repro details from them: curl against /v1/realtime/generate, model=cedar-extended-8k, long clinical note -> p95 spike. Request id examples: r-0a1b2c3d, r-0a1b2c4e.

deploy-bot: deploy: byte-encoder v2 cutover -> realtime-pool-3 at 2026-03-15T16:22:30Z (sha: bb7f3a).

kai_runtime: thanks. grabbing traces + tokenization histograms now. can someone paste a short repro payload?

anna_support: pasted minimal repro they used: 
```
{
  "model": "cedar-extended-8k",
  "input": "<~6.5k chars omitted for thread>\n        [long clinical note repeated to hit >4k tokens]"
}
```
They also said adding header `x-use-legacy-tokenizer: true` drops p95 back to ~500ms.

sam_oncall: confirmed in tracing — majority of added latency is in tokenization step (tokenizer-service call). Before cutover tokenization ~40-80ms; after cutover some requests show 1.2s stuck in tokenization, tail scales with length. KV/cache and generation times look normal.

kai_runtime: investigating tokenization vnode logs now. I see a regex-based boundary scan in byte-encoder v2 that iterates on long buffers. For inputs with many punctuation clusters it's degenerating (O(n^2) in worst case). reproducer attached to tracing: trace://traces/34567/r-0a1b2c3d.

maria_pm: ouch. are there affected customers we should auto-rollback for? maplehealth is in prod, high volume.

kai_runtime: we can enable per-customer fallback to legacy encoder (fast to flip) — flag: `tokenizer_fallback=legacy` in routing rule. I can push that to their org in 5m. Also rolling back global cutover would be 20m ops time.

anna_support: customer asked for mitigation ASAP. they said they can wait 10–15m for fix.

sam_oncall: +1 fallback route. also setting a short-term autoscale to avoid queuing to mask tail while we patch.

kai_runtime: adding steps here:
1) set routing rule for org: maplehealth -> tokenizer_fallback=legacy (runtime flag).
2) enable temporary autoscale bump on realtime-pool-3 to reduce head-of-line queuing.
3) create hotfix branch to replace the worst regex path with streaming scanner (patch target: tokenizer/byte_encoder/scanner.cc).
4) run canary on small orgs, then global cutover after patch.

anna_support: repro command I gave customer to test fallback: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/realtime/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "x-use-legacy-tokenizer: true" \
  -d '{"model":"cedar-extended-8k","input":"<large note>"}'
```
They confirmed p95 back to ~480ms with that header.

maria_pm: please confirm impact window and comms plan. we'll send a short status to MapleHealth and note rollback plan if fallback doesn't hold.

kai_runtime: doing the flip for MapleHealth now. I'll post logs + postmortem stub here.

kai_runtime: done — routing rule applied, verifies: maplehealth tokenization time dropped to ~350–520ms. sample request r-0a1b2c3d now completes in 520ms.

sam_oncall: autoscale bumped, no queuing currently. monitoring p95 in Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rt/tokenizer-latency. setting alert for >900ms.

anna_support: sent customer note: "We identified a regression in the new byte-encoder cutover affecting long inputs. We've switched your org to the legacy tokenizer while we push a bugfix. We'll follow up with ETA for a permanent fix." :thumbsup:

maria_pm: ETA on patch?

kai_runtime: hotfix PR created, running unit + e2e. hoping to have canary by EOD. root cause is the boundary regex being applied repeatedly on long multi-byte sequences; streaming scanner fix reduces complexity to O(n).

anna_support: adding this thread to ticket #T-4729. will update MapleHealth when canary looks good.

sam_oncall: follow-ups: add a regression test for >8k char inputs to CI, add a perf gate on tokenizer-sdk cutovers, and document `x-use-legacy-tokenizer` header as emergency workaround.

kai_runtime: agreed. I'll include the perf regression graphs and trace links in the postmortem.

anna_support: thanks all — closing loop with customer after canary.
